Subject: Monthly KPI packet: owner confirmations + QBR slide assignments

Team — attaching the November KPI packet (monthly_kpi_dashboard_v3.xlsx) and the current QBR slide template. High level: latency P50 slipped 8% in the last two weeks, token cost increased by ~12% MoM, uptime steady at 99.96%, and usage growth is mostly from two new sandbox accounts (BrightEdge and ACME PoC).

I need the following before I consolidate the QBR readout on Tuesday: 
- Metric owners to confirm numbers in the sheet and call out any data-quality caveats (deadline: EOD Monday).
- A short note per metric (1–2 bullets) with root cause hypothesis and proposed mitigation.
- Slide owner volunteers: who will own the latency deck, cost economics slide, uptime/incident summary, and customer usage narrative?

Specific asks: 
- @irene_choi: please validate the latency P50/P95 series and confirm whether the testbed rollout last week affected production buckets.
- @markus_klein: can you pull a quick cost delta by model and quantization state? If we need a short-term mitigation, list the quick wins.
- @tessa_morgan: update the uptime blameless summary if there were any postmortem notes.
- @laura_bennett: consolidate slide owners and schedule the dry run.

Naomi / ACME procurement — including you on visibility. If any numbers here affect your renewal conversation, flag and we can call out in the QBR.

Thanks,
Olga

Thanks Olga — quick notes after skimming the sheet:
- Latency: the P50 jump aligns with a canary of the batched-attention kernel (deployed 11/01) that under certain micro-batch sizes returns slightly higher tail for short prompts. Confirmed impact on 2% of requests (internal routing to testpool leaked to a small subset). I'll attach the raw trace IDs in the drive link.
- Data caveat: the default aggregation used the 30d rolling window; for QBR we'd want to show both 7d and 30d to highlight the recent regression.

Proposed mitigation (short-term): rollback kernel to previous release on the affected shard group and enable per-customer routing to avoid regressions for premium contracts. Medium-term: add micro-batch size heuristics to kernel selector.

I'll update the latency slide draft and own the latency deck for the QBR.

Irene
Irene Choi | Director, Service Reliability
Redwood Inference

Looping in a brief cost readout: I ran the token-cost delta by model for Oct→Nov and attached a short CSV in the drive (cost_breakdown_oct_nov.csv). Key points: 
- 12% MoM increase primarily from higher usage on large-context customers + a small increase in per-token runtime due to the same kernel changes Irene called out.
- Quantization-eligible models account for 28% of tokens. Moving an initial subset to int8-q8 can net ~18% per-token reduction for those flows.
- Short-term quick wins: enable prefix caching for repeat prompts (estimated 6% saving for BrightEdge test queries), and restrict high-priced variants to dedicated-reserved paths during peak hours.

I'm happy to draft the cost slide and recommend a proposed rollout timeline for quantization and caching changes. I can share an A/B plan to validate no quality regressions.

-Markus
Markus Klein | VP, Product — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
attachments: cost_breakdown_oct_nov.csv
